counterexamples.before: Real worker exits and is reaped. An unknown session directory entry makes Remove fail. Reap/STOP retries signal the retired PGID, then ECHILD prevents cleanup forever.
counterexamples.after: Remember kill/reap stages; keep owner/interface and replay guards; retry only filesystem removal. No retired-group signal, foreign STOP or conflicting admission.

counterexamples.before: Shutdown clears jobs unconditionally even if real directory removal failed.
counterexamples.after: Keep failed jobs, return false, permit later shutdown/removal retry. Supervisor returns exit 5 when its explicit shutdown still fails.

platform_limits: macOS supplies only the missing prctl API as an explicit no-op double. fork, waitid/waitpid, groups, signals and filesystem operations are real.
The initial ProcessStart assertion is Linux-only because macOS has no /proc. The post-teardown identity rejection is checked on both hosts.
Signal attempts are counted and forwarded to the real kernel; this proves absence of repeated signalling, not real PID-reuse behavior.
No actual FFRT, service IPC, OpenVPN TLS or TUN runtime was exercised.

root_linux_tests.expected: 6 tests; actual prctl/subreaper/PDEATHSIG and /proc identity. No source/out mounts or writes.
